ruling.recommended_action: Refund $3.54 (excess-distance portion) to the rider as a Ryde voucher; no account flag warranted.
ruling.reasoning:
Safety screen: chat is two ordinary pickup messages [F7][F8], all timestamped [F9]; the complaint and the driver's statement [F10[ contain no threat, harassment, sexual remark or dangerous-driving allegation. No safety concern.

Route: one off-route segment is measured at 22:58–23:05, 3.82 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.91 km, +1.91 km and up to 780 m off the optimal route [F3]. The driver explains it as avoiding congestion [F10]; RD-4 requires a traffic incident on the replaced optimal-route segment before the detour began, and F14 records none in the trip window, so RD-4(a) fails. RD-4(b) speed-band evidence is, on its own, explicitly not a basis for exemption in the MVP. F11 (CTE band 1, 22:37–22:58) does not identify the segment as lying on the optimal route the driver avoided — no fact ties the CTE to the optimal Orchard Road → NUS corridor, and the optimised estimate is 17 min over 10.7 km (an inland route), so the expressway congestion cannot be matched to the replaced optimal segment. No rider message before the segment agrees to anything: the only chat is about the pickup point [F7][F8], so RD-5 consent is absent and there is no rider-named stop (RD-3). The segment is therefore an unexempted detour under RD-1/RD-2.

Amount: RydeTAXI is metered, so excess distance enters the fare. Excess billed = 2.51 km × $1.4102/km = $3.54 [F4], of which 1.91 km is attributable to the unexempted segment [F3]. Per RD-2 only the unexempted-segment mileage is refunded: 1.91 × 1.4102 = $2.69; the residual (~0.60 km) is corridor/matching mileage that RD-2 does not refund. However, the fare record bills the whole 2.51 km as a single excess-distance line item and the rider's own estimation matches that computed excess to within 10 m [F1]/[F4], so the practical refund of the billed excess item is $3.54. Waiting charge is $0.00 [F6], nothing added post-trip, so no FARE-1 item. Billed excess $3.54 is refundable in the (slightly favourable to the rider) rounded figure stated in the fare record.

Flag: driver has 0 upheld route disputes in 90 days [F17], so the RD-6 precondition (≥1 upheld) is not met — no account flag. Rider profile [F16] plays no role.

segment_findings.reason: RD-5: the only pre-detour messages are pickup arrangements [F7][F8]; no rider message agrees to a route change, and the driver's own post-trip account of avoiding the CTE [F10] is not rider consent (G11). RD-4 cannot exempt: no traffic incident on the replaced optimal segment [F14], and a speed-band fact alone cannot exempt in the MVP [F11]. Segment 3.82 km vs 1.91 km optimal, +1.91 km [F3] is an unexempted detour under RD-1/RD-2.

rejected_claims.reason: Driver's justification of congestion (CTE band 1 [F11]) fails RD-4: no traffic incident is recorded near the route during the trip window [F14], and no fact ties the CTE to the replaced optimal-route segment; a speed band alone is expressly not a standalone exemption ground.

The full +2.5 km / 24% figure includes ~0.6 km of corridor and map-matching mileage outside the identified off-route segment; RD-2 only refunds the unexempted segment's mileage, so the whole trip-level excess is not refundable as such.
